# Jubilees Chapter 14 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** The Covenant Between the Pieces; Abram's Vision; Covenant Sealed

---

**14:1** After these things, in the fourth year of this week, on the new moon of the third month, the word of the LORD came to Abram in a dream, saying: "Do not be afraid, Abram; I am your shield and your very great reward."

**14:2** He said: "LORD, what will you give me, since I am going away childless, and the son of Masek, my maidservant's son — Eliezer of Damascus — will be my heir? You have given me no offspring."

**14:3** He said to him: "This man shall not be your heir; the one who comes from your own body shall be your heir."

**14:4** He brought him outside and said: "Look up at the sky and count the stars, if you are able to count them."

**14:5** He looked up at the sky and saw the stars, and a word was said to him: "So shall your descendants be."

**14:6** And he believed the LORD, and it was reckoned to him as righteousness.

**14:7** He said to him: "I am the LORD who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldees to give you this land to inherit."

**14:8** He said: "LORD God, how am I to know that I will inherit it?"

**14:9** He said to him: "Bring me a heifer three years old, a she-goat three years old, a ram three years old, a turtledove, and a young pigeon."

**14:10** He took all these in the middle of the month and dwelt by the oak of Mamre, near Hebron.

**14:11** He built an altar there and sacrificed all these animals. He poured their blood on the altar, divided them in the middle, and placed each piece across from the other; but the birds he did not divide.

**14:12** Birds came down upon the pieces, but Abram drove them away and would not allow them to touch the offering.

**14:13** As the sun was going down, a deep sleep fell upon Abram, and a great dark dread came over him.

**14:14** It was said to Abram: "Know for certain that your descendants will be aliens in a land not their own, and will be enslaved and afflicted for four hundred years."

**14:15** "But I will also judge the nation they serve, and afterward they will come out with great possessions."

**14:16** "As for you, you will go to your ancestors in peace; you will be buried at a good old age."

**14:17** "And in the fourth generation they will return here, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete."

**14:18** He awoke from his sleep and arose; the sun had set, and there was a flame — behold, a smoking furnace and a flaming torch passed between the pieces.

**14:19** On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram, saying: "To your descendants I have given this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates: the Kenites, the Kenizzites, the Kadmonites, the Perizzites, the Rephaim, the Phiblites, the Hivites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites."

**14:20** The day passed, and Abram offered the pieces and the birds with their grain offerings and their drink offerings, and the fire consumed them all.

**14:21** On that day we made a covenant with Abram, just as we had covenanted with Noah in this same month; and Abram renewed the festival and its ordinance for himself forever.

**14:22** Abram rejoiced and made all these things known to Sarai his wife. He believed that he would have offspring, but she did not yet bear.

**14:23** Sarai counseled her husband Abram and said to him: "Go in to Hagar, my Egyptian maidservant; perhaps through her I may obtain children." Abram listened to Sarai his wife and said to her: "Do as you think best."

**14:24** Sarai took Hagar her maidservant and gave her to Abram her husband as a wife, and Abram went in to her.

---
*SOPHIA notes: Consensus follows LOGOS throughout. The third-month covenant (v.1, v.21) preserving the Jubilees theological structure — same month as Noah's covenant and the Feast of Weeks. "Great dark dread" (v.13) follows LOGOS "great dark dread"; PNEUMA's "terrifying, smothering" is vivid but over-descriptive. "Phiblites" (v.19) preserved as Jubilees-unique variant.*
